newsitem.title: USA: Fire causes power dip for New York City.
newsitem.headline: Fire causes power dip for New York City.

text.p: A fire at a power substation in Yonkers on Wednesday morning caused a system-wide dip in electrical voltage for New York City and Westchester County, utility officials said.
"All of our customers felt the dip," said Mike Spall, spokesman for Consolidated Edison Co. of New York. "The system stabilised. It acted as it's designed to do."
He said that when the four-alarm fire broke out at about 9 a.m., power was diverted from the other approximately one dozen substations that supply the system.
No actual outages occurred and no further power dips were expected, Spall said. No injuries were reported in fire that was "largely controlled" by 11 a.m., he said. An oil fire remained, he said.
In a momentary power dip, "lights will flicker, computers might flicker, computers might go down," another Con Ed spokesman said.
In the late morning rush hour, Long Island Railroad reported 15 minute delays because of electrical problems in its signals and third rails.
The New York and American Stock Exchanges opened on time at 9:30 a.m.
"We took a power hit at 9 a.m., but otherwise everything is fine," said a spokeswoman for Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
